subject: Opterra renewal: capacity rescope, tier changes and rate-limit plan
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@opterra.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Holt <marcus.holt@opterra.io>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + uplift planning: we need a larger commit and a rateband change

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. As discussed, usage for our generative assist flows jumped again in March; I'm attaching the March export so you can see the delta. We want to lock in a renewal today but need two changes to the current hosted plan:

- Increase committed monthly tokens from 800M -> 1.5B
- Move to the next rateband for sustained usage and get a clear soft-throttle policy (we saw a few 429s last quarter)

We also need the renewal to include a phased rollout for a higher rate-limit (burst and sustained) over 60 days — Ops needs that window to validate throughput. Procurement (procurement@opterra.io) will need an exec-approved SOW and final invoice.

Attached: Opterra_Mar2028_usage.csv (summary + top routes).

Can you send a proposed quote + a mutual action plan by EOD Wednesday?

—Lena
Lena Park
Head of Product Integrations, Opterra
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@opterra.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + uplift planning: we need a larger commit and a rateband change

Lena — thanks for the details and the export. High level response: we can support the 1.5B monthly commit and present a tiered rateband that reduces unit price once consumption crosses 1B tokens/month.

Quick items:
- I'll put together a price summary and an SOW draft for a 24-month renewal with a 60-day phased rate-limit ramp.
- Marissa, can you prepare an initial quote (Excel) with the commit/overage buckets and the proposed discount schedule?
- Priya, we'll need a short ops-runbook describing the phased rollout (60d) and automatic fallback to current commit if latency/regressions occur.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Wednesday 10:00am PT to review numbers and the rollout plan. Does that work for you?

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2028 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + uplift planning: draft quote and rateband options attached

Team — draft attached (Proposed_Uplift_Quote.xlsx). Summary:

- Option A (24mo): 1.5B commit / month, 35% unit discount above baseline, soft throttle threshold at 2.5x sustained burst => recommended for predictable unit economics.
- Option B (12mo): 1.5B commit / month, 25% discount, higher overage rate but lower commitment term.
- Overage pricing and emergency burst pockets called out in the spreadsheet.

Questions for product/ops: what is the expected latency delta at the 2.5x burst ceiling? Also need a confirmation of the soft-throttle behavior (how aggressively we drop token throughput vs prioritizing latency).

Attachments: Proposed_Uplift_Quote.xlsx

—Marissa
Director, Renewals & GTM Deals, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@opterra.io>, procurement@opterra.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2028 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Opterra renewal: proposed SOW, rollout timeline and DocuSign

Lena / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a first-pass SOW (Opterra_Renewal_SOW_v2.pdf) and a link to the DocuSign envelope for signature: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/OPTR-2028-04

Key highlights from the SOW & quote:
- Term: 24 months starting 2028-05-01
- Commit: 1.5B tokens / month (monthly billing)
- Pricing: see attached quote (Option A recommended) with progressive unit pricing after 1B tokens/month
- Phased rollout: 60-day ramp window. Day 0–14: burst testing up to 1.2x baseline; Day 15–45: incremental ramp to 2.0x sustained; Day 46–60: validate 2.5x sustained for short bursts with ops runbook engaged.
- Soft-throttle: requests that exceed configured QoS will receive 429 after burst window — ops will preferentially shed non-critical routes first.

Ops & Delivery (Priya + Jordan) will run a pre-cutover validation checklist prior to Day 0. Marissa and I will manage commercial/PO and invoicing.

If the SOW looks good, please sign via DocuSign and we'll schedule a technical kickoff with Priya and Jordan.

Karthik
From: Marcus Holt <marcus.holt@opterra.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@opterra.io>, procurement@opterra.io
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Opterra renewal: proposed SOW, rollout timeline and DocuSign

Karthik —

Quick notes from Ops/Procurement after an internal review:
- We prefer a 90-day validation window rather than 60 (Ops risk tolerance). Can you accommodate a 90d phased ramp, with a mid-point checkpoint to review performance and safety metrics?
- Procurement has two redlines on the SOW (attached): 1) clause on data retention and log access; 2) SLA credits for repeated soft-throttle events. I've attached a redlined SOW.
- They also need SOC2 Type II evidence and our security questionnaire completed before signing.

Can you push an updated SOW and confirm whether the 90d ramp affects pricing?

—Marcus
VP, Engineering Ops, Opterra
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Holt <marcus.holt@opterra.io>, Lena Park <lena.park@opterra.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Opterra renewal: proposed SOW, rollout timeline and DocuSign

Marcus / Lena —

Thanks for the redlines and the ask on SOC2. We can accept a 90-day phased validation instead of 60 — ops will add a formal mid-point checkpoint at Day 45 to review SLAs, latency and error budgets. That does not change the published commercial pricing; we will keep the 24-month term and 1.5B commit.

Responses to redlines:
- Data retention/log access: we'll include a specific appendix that confirms log retention windows and the mechanism for secure access (KMS-protected export + timeboxed access).
- SLA credits for repeated soft-throttle: we can add a credit schedule that triggers if soft-throttle events exceed agreed thresholds in a 30-day window — draft language attached in the updated SOW.

Attachments: Opterra_Renewal_SOW_v2_redline.pdf (contains the appendix and SLA-credit language), updated ops-runbook (internal).

Next steps:
1) We'll upload the revised SOW to DocuSign by EOD Thursday.
2) Procurement can share a PO upon signature; Marissa will trigger invoicing and any pro-rated adjustments.
3) Schedule technical kickoff for Week of 2028-05-06 (Priya/Jordan).

If that aligns, Karthik — please confirm and I'll finalize the DocuSign envelope.

—Priya
Solutions & Delivery, Redwood Inference
